mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates on equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which suppresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.5%, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits above 1.65 million units signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives higher corporate revenues and earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1.65 million, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and rise in the unemployment rate signals a weakening manufacturing sector and labor market contraction, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both INDPRO < 113.0 and UNRATE > 4.5%, or the joint signal fails to generate a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPIAUCSL above 203.5 combined with a stable federal funds rate signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting the Fed to delay rate cuts, which increases real rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 203.5 and FEDFUNDS ≤ 5.5%, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 365 billion dollars signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate sales and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS exceeds 365 billion, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll employment above 135,600 thousand, combined with a declining unemployment rate, signals a strong labor market that increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 135600 and UNRATE < 4.7%, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth above 2.0% annualized, as measured by GDPC1, signals strong economic momentum that supports corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of quarters when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
